title: Showcase: the story of sprint 1
summary: Assemble a talk from real Maker's Log beats, give it live to the family, then run this week's Sprout card to teach someone younger.
materials: your Maker's Log entries from weeks 1 to 3

steps.title: Mine the log for beats
steps.body:
This talk is not written from memory, it is mined from your Maker's Log. Open your entries from weeks 1 to 3 and hunt for three beats.

Beat one: the first time the copper obeyed. Maybe the moment the AND gate held its light back until both buttons agreed. Beat two: the fight. The bug that took the longest, told proudly, like a scientist reporting from the field: what you expected, what happened instead, what finally found it. Beat three: the payoff. The adder answering before anyone can check it, and why it never misses.

Read the exact words you wrote on those days. A line written the day of the bug is worth ten lines remembered a month later. If a log entry makes you wince a little, that is the good one.

The same three rules as every talk: speak to the back wall, one pause on purpose, look at one person per sentence.

steps.title: Assemble and rehearse
steps.body:
Build the talk from the three beats in order: the first obedience, the fight, the machine that cannot miss. Give each beat two or three sentences, no more.

Close with one line about what comes next: the gift page is open, and the family's ideas from the build showcase are already on it. Do not name a person. The person gets named at week 8, and a good season keeps its secrets on schedule.

Practise twice with a timer running. Ninety seconds is the ceiling.
checklist: Three beats, each lifted from a real log entry
Under 90 seconds, with one pause on purpose
Ends on the gift page, without naming anyone

steps.title: Teach someone younger
steps.body:
A parent card is the short card in the app that a grown-up normally uses with Sprout. It has a title, a few steps to do together, and two or three things to notice.

This week you run it, not a grown-up. Open this week's Sprout parent card and read it all the way through before you start, so you know where it is going.

Then run it with a younger sibling, cousin or friend, or a parent playing the part. This one lives outdoors and is played entirely by ear, so your job is to say the prompts, walk beside them, and listen hard to what they hear. Let them make every find themselves, even the slow ones, especially the slow ones.

Watch for one thing they do that surprises you: a sound they catch that you missed, or a find you would never have picked.
checklist: They made the finds themselves, and I did not make any for them.
I noticed one thing they did that surprised me

steps.title: Record it
steps.prompt: Record the live talk, phone propped up, whole face in frame. Keep rolling for the family's questions if they have any.
